This application was presented at a meeting of the Anti-infective Drugs' Advisory Committee on April 5, 2011.

recommendation.text: On whether safety and effectiveness had been demonstrated, the committee voted 13 Yes / 0 No / 0 Abstain. On a second question about the clinical significance of the lower recurrence rate at Day 31, the vote was split 6 Yes / 6 No / 1 Abstain.

quote.quote: On the question of whether safety and effectiveness had been demonstrated for fidaxomicin the committee voted 13 Yes; 0 No; 0 Abstain.

linkages.concern: The committee's discussion noted that very few of the studied subjects had prior episodes of CDAD, and at the meeting the applicant indicated a trial of fidaxomicin in patients with multiple previous CDAD recurrences had been planned.
linkages.change: A postmarketing commitment (PMC) was agreed: a prospective, randomized, comparative trial to demonstrate efficacy of Dificid in patients with multiple recurrences of CDAD. The sparse prior-episode data was also to be noted in the label.

concern_quote.quote: Important points of discussion included the fact that very few of studied subjects had prior episodes of CDAD, which should be noted in the label and considered for a PMC.

change_quote.quote: Conduct a prospective, randomized, comparative trial to demonstrate the efficacy of Dificid (fidaxomicin) in the treatment of patients with multiple recurrences of *C. difficile*-associated diarrhea.

linkages.concern: Raised in the advisory committee discussion (the statistical reviewer presented concerns about the claims for reduced recurrence, and the committee split 6-6-1 on the clinical significance of the lower Day-31 recurrence rate), there were concerns about the claims for recurrence.
linkages.change: On that basis the review team did not grant the requested 'reduction in recurrence' claim and proposed a narrower indication limited to treatment of Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD).

summary: Fidaxomicin (Dificid, NDA 201699) was reviewed by the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee on April 5, 2011. The committee voted unanimously (13-0-0) that safety and effectiveness were demonstrated for treatment of CDAD, but split 6-6-1 on the clinical significance of the lower Day-31 recurrence rate, with members uncomfortable with the 'recurrence'/'global cure' terminology. Reflecting that discussion, the review team declined the requested 'reduction in recurrence' claim and approved a narrower CDAD indication, and a postmarketing commitment was agreed to study fidaxomicin in patients with multiple CDAD recurrences.
